title: Dedicated capacity intake: request-to-activation choreography and safety hedges
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As we scale Dedicated offerings, onboarding requests vary widely in traffic shape and risk. Current intake captures capacity numbers but lacks a deterministic flow that ties request sizing, approval SLA, autoscale policy defaults, and fleet-level guardrails into a single activation choreography. This ticket defines the request-to-activation choreography and safety hedges so we can reduce provisioning time, avoid overcommit, and ensure throughput guarantees are enforceable across fleet operations.

Goals: 1) Define a deterministic intake form and validation rules that produce a recommended throughput profile and autoscale tier. 2) Specify approval lanes, timeboxes, and escalation rules for high-risk requests. 3) Produce operator-runbook steps to validate an activation and rollback safely. 4) Implement a lightweight policy layer that enforces minimum safety hedges at activation (cost caps, canary percent, fallback routes).

Scope: This ticket covers the product-flow and operational playbook. It includes UX for intake, approval rubric, autoscale defaults mapping, and the gate checks at activation. Implementation tasks (builders for the UI and autoscale engine) are separate engineering tickets referenced as sub_issues. Non-goals: deep pricing contracts, legal SOWs, and on-prem installation packaging are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: A structured intake schema exists and maps raw customer inputs (peak rps, 99th latency SLO, model mix, region) to a recommended throughput profile and autoscale tier.
Clear approval lanes documented: self-serve, SME review, executive sign-off, with SLA timeboxes and required artifacts for each lane.
Activation playbook created for operators: pre-activation checks, canary rollout steps, smoke-test checklist, and automated rollback triggers.
Safety hedges implemented as policy definitions: cost cap, initial canary at <=10% traffic, automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or region.
Runbook validated with 2 internal dry-run activations and observed metrics dashboard links created for post-activation verification.
Handoff packet (intake form + approval evidence + activation log template) is available in the Confluence onboarding space.
Security review completed and signed off for gating controls (KMS integration and audit log requirements).
tasks: Draft intake schema and mapping table
Prototype policy definitions for cost caps and canary enforcement
Coordinate two dry-run activations with internal teams
Submit for security review and compliance sign-off
notes: Decision: We will prefer conservative autoscale defaults for first 90 days of GA for any high-variance traffic customers.
Trade-off: Tight canary and cost caps increase manual work for high-throughput customers but reduce blast radius during rollout.
Open question: Should approval lane require a signed technical runbook for customers expecting >5x typical spikes? (TBD with sales)
Design constraint: Intake form must be concise (<= 6 fields) to keep self-serve conversion high; complex sizing moved to optional advanced step.
